key_insight: TDFold reformulates 3D protein structure prediction as a 2D image‑like diffusion on geometric templates, enabling more accurate, faster and more efficient single‑sequence folding than leading models.
problem_solved: Accurately predicting 3D protein structures from a single amino‑acid sequence without relying on multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) or heavy compute; reducing inference time and resource requirements while improving prediction quality.
method: Encode sequence-derived pairwise geometry (distances/angles) as 2D image‑like geometric templates.
Apply a 2D geometric template diffusion model that denoises and iteratively refines these pairwise maps.
Reconstruct 3D coordinates from the refined 2D geometry using a lightweight pipeline optimized for single‑sequence inputs, yielding faster inference and improved accuracy.
impact: Enables accurate, high‑throughput protein structure prediction in resource‑constrained settings and simplifies integration into ML-driven design and screening pipelines by removing MSA dependence and cutting compute cost.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Sequence → 2D geometric template (distance/angle map) → 2D diffusion denoising → 3D coordinate reconstruction
Progression heatmaps: before/after denoising of pairwise geometry (showing noise removal over diffusion steps)
Bar chart: accuracy and inference time comparison vs. leading models (e.g., AlphaFold2, other single‑sequence methods)
Icon set: single‑sequence input, diffusion process (noise → clean), lightning bolt for speed/efficiency
paper_title: Two-dimensional geometric template diffusion for boosting single-sequence protein structure prediction
paper_authors: Xudong Wang, Tong Zhang, Zhen Cui, Xu Guo, Fuyun Wang
